findings.finding: Parent acceptance criterion 5 ('Every client-facing change carries a release-notes line') is only PARTIALLY covered: the overlay-warning story (f5f5) introduces a client-facing deprecation — client projects' .rebar/criteria_routing.json files using the legacy `activate:` id-list form will now emit a deprecation warning scheduled for removal in v1.0.0 — but f5f5 adds no docs/release-notes.md entry, and no sibling adds one for it.
scenarios: Parent completion verifier asserts 'every client-facing change carries a release-notes line'; the newly client-facing overlay deprecation has none, so the parent AC fails even after all five children land.
A downstream client upgrading sees a new deprecation warning on their criteria_routing.json with no release-note explaining the v1.0.0 removal timeline.
findings.suggested_fix: Add docs/release-notes.md to f5f5's file_impact and an approach step adding a line such as: 'Deprecation: the legacy `"activate": ["<id>"]` id-list form in .rebar/criteria_routing.json now logs a one-time deprecation warning (scheduled for removal in v1.0.0); use the mapping form.' Optionally add an AC asserting the line's presence.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH had no remaining disable consumers (A/B concluded on 'always on') and note the removal in release notes as the back-out signal, or give a short deprecation window.
evidence: AC3: 'REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH is gone with prefetch always on'
Context frames it as 'a finished A/B env var' but does not state whether the disable path had live consumers
findings.finding: Removing REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH with 'prefetch always on' silently drops an opt-out: any consumer currently setting REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH=0 to disable prefetch will have that value ignored with no transition or rollback note.
scenarios: A caller relying on REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH=0 to suppress prefetch loses that control after the env var is removed

evidence: AC3: 'REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH is gone with prefetch always on'
Context names 'severity residue from ADR 0108' and 'private re-exports that ADR 0111 forbids' and 'a finished A/B env var'
ABSENCE: the plan's only documentation surface is the per-story release-notes line (criterion 5); nothing audits whether ADR 0108/0111 text or env-var docs reference the now-deleted artifacts.
findings.finding: The plan removes the documented `REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH` environment variable (prefetch becomes always-on) and deletes artifacts tied to ADR 0108 (severity) and ADR 0111 (private re-exports), but does not state whether any docs, ADRs, or references to these removed artifacts/config get updated, risking stranded stale references.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria 3 and Context / Problem (ADR 0108 severity residue, ADR 0111 private re-exports, REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH)
scenarios: A reader consults docs/ADR 0108 and finds it still describing severity-driven gate policy that no longer exists.
A user searches docs for REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH after the env var is removed and finds stale guidance.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the relevant stories a grep for ADR 0108/0111 and REBAR_VERIFY_PREFETCH references across docs/, and update or note-as-completed any doc that mentions the removed artifacts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the scaffolding story, name provider_parity.py as a live importer of fidelity_spot_eval and specify where `_majority_decision`/`_verdict_decision` relocate (shared module) so deleting the spot-eval harness does not break the provider-parity harness's import.
evidence: Plan: 'a spot-eval harness with an unreachable entry point' and 'the spot-eval harness ... are deleted with their only importers migrated.'
src/rebar/llm/evals/provider_parity.py:52-57 imports `_majority_decision as majority_decision` and `_verdict_decision as verdict_decision` from rebar.llm.plan_review.fidelity_spot_eval.
provider_parity.py:50-51 comment: 'Single-sourced from the spot-eval precedent so both harnesses score verdicts identically; a local copy would make their recorded evidence incomparable.'

provider_parity.py:1-12 docstring establishes it as a distinct, standing operator-run harness (not scaffolding, not the spot-eval, not slated for deletion) that deliberately reuses fidelity_spot_eval's `_verdict_decision`/`_majority_decision` mappings 'so the two harnesses stay comparable.'
The harness's entry point may be unreachable, but the MODULE has a live symbol-level importer; a naive deletion breaks provider_parity at import time.
findings.finding: Deleting the spot-eval harness (fidelity_spot_eval.py) will break the live provider-parity harness, which imports two helpers from it; the plan's generic 'only importers migrated' clause does not name this cross-module importer or where the shared verdict mappings relocate.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, criterion 2 ('the spot-eval harness ... deleted with their only importers migrated'); Child decomposition, 'Cutover scaffolding story'
scenarios: Scaffolding story deletes fidelity_spot_eval.py and provider_parity.py raises ImportError on `from rebar.llm.plan_review.fidelity_spot_eval import ...`.
Operator runs the provider-parity harness after the cutover and it fails to import.
findings.suggested_fix: Relocate `_verdict_decision`/`_majority_decision` to a surviving shared module (e.g. rebar.llm.parity or a small shared decision-mapping module) and repoint provider_parity.py's import there, then delete only the unreachable spot-eval entry point and its own private surface. State this importer and relocation target explicitly in the scaffolding story so the 'only importers migrated' claim is concrete.
